item: OSM: a stored monthly summary of the planet's prior, built when a history cut finishes (v0.6.0, R435)
key_paths: src/osm/prior_summary.py; src/osm/lane_models.py; src/osm/history.py; src/osm/trends.py; src/osm/profile.py; src/api/osm_lane.py; src/static/app-map.js; tests/test_osm_prior_summary.py; tests/osm_prior_summary_node_test.js
summary: The readers of the planet's past (tag adoption, openings and closures, brands, channels, freshness) grouped a country's whole history table by month on every request, about a minute at 12M history rows. When a history cut finishes, one pass now stores the same aggregate rows (osm_history_monthly, headed by osm_history_summaries, stamped with the cut's finished_at and a digest of the counting rules); a read selects a few hundred rows. The stored rows are exactly what the computed path hands the series builders, a summary is used only when both stamps match, and any other state computes from the history and says so on the page (prior.source, prior.summary.state). A cut that already exists, or a lane cut by an older build with no such tables, gets its summary from a POST (a GET never writes), asked for once per country per session by the page. Measured on the synthetic Germany-scale lane (12M history rows): the four surfaces took 115 s, they take 9.8 s now (what remains is the unchanged snapshot and window reads), the prior step itself is 0.7 to 5 ms, one build is 80 s; the two paths answer identically on all four surfaces.
